note: Level 0, L.O.S.T.'s level (lineage B02: refinement v3). Its one definition: the server reads it (src/frameworks/lost/server/sim.level0.js, given it by the sim's composition, src/core/server/sim.js) and the page's compiled client is built with it (src/core/client/game/shared/world.ts, through level-data.cjs). The map is cols x rows cells of 96 px; rooms, corridors (carved), partitions (walls inside the rooms, blocked), doorways (carved through them) and pits (floor voids that do not block sight) are in cells, [x, y, w, h] or {x, y}; the PILLAR HALL's pillars are squares of size px centred on every one of the columns x rows cell positions (half = size / 2); the spawn is a cell; the anchor is the open cell beside it (the spawn is hard against a wall) from which the server checks that a place is reachable (its monsters' spawn spots and the glitched walls: N.A.N.I.'s sim.ai.js, which wrote it as {x:1056,y:3264} until C4c; the page does not use it); blackouts: the first after first s, each one length + (its number % lengthCycle) s long, the next gap + (its number % gapCycle) x gapStep s after the last ends. world.js holds the damaged walls, the pass-through windows, the props and the lamps (WORLD.carve, WORLD.lamps), carved and placed after this map. A change here changes the level on both sides: the gate compares both with B++ (its sim, page, bundle and port steps).
